anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither fact moved: both outputs keep P1 and P2 open, write nothing, and leave the spec's acceptance row and constant-time design intact. The notable drift in After is not in these facts but in the handling path: Before treats the requested rewording as a contract-narrowing proposal and records a paused contract exception with an accept/preserve menu, whereas After explicitly says 'No contract exception is recorded' and routes a request to drop the design mechanism to 'description repair' (then concludes there is nothing to repair). That classification is internally odd — a rewording that removes a spec Design sentence is exactly the narrowing the contract-exception path exists for — and it undercuts the consent-contract-change-stop scenarios the Change says it preserves. To keep the new course model while retaining Before's safety, have the change-request classification still check the proposed wording against the contract: if it removes a spec-owned requirement, record the contract exception and render the contract menu (accept contract change / preserve contract [recommended] / stop) instead of the plain initial template; only genuinely scope-neutral rewordings should route to description repair under course deliver.
